⚠️ Trump Backs Down Once Again From a Threatened Military Escalation

Trump appeared to back down once again from a threatened military escalation against Tehran, offering fresh fodder to the narrative Iranian officials are eager to promote: they are not the ones who fear war — Trump is.

Iran’s leadership believes it has found the world’s Achilles’ heel. With the help of regional militia allies, Tehran spent the past week underscoring its ability to threaten several of the world’s most critical energy facilities and waterways.

It has continued to raise the stakes in its confrontation with Washington over when and how to stop the renewed hostilities and return to a short-lived agreement to begin peace negotiations, which collapsed last month.

When Trump signaled in recent days that a major escalation was imminent if no concessions were made, two former Iranian officials said Tehran’s leadership told him to go right ahead.

“They are ready for war, and they won’t back down,” 
said Amir al-Mousawi, a former Iranian diplomat, who said he had met over the weekend with the team surrounding Iran’s chief negotiator and Speaker of Parliament, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf.

Al-Mousawi described an exchange of messages between U.S. and Iranian officials sent over the weekend through Pakistani and Qatari officials. He said Trump vowed a severe attack on civilian infrastructure, such as power plants, if Iran did not restart negotiations.

The Iranians refused, he said, unless Washington returned to the previously agreed “memorandum of understanding,”
 which many experts say was favorable to Iran.

“We have no problem with war at all, and we are ready for the big confrontation,” 
al-Mousawi said the Iranians told the Americans.
“Trump told the Iranians: ‘I will hit the power in Iran.’ So, the Iranians said: ‘If you strike, we strike.’”

The official Saudi news channel said on Sunday that Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, the de facto ruler of Saudi Arabia, had recently spoken with Trump to stress “the necessity of prioritizing dialogue to de-escalate tensions” and “prevent a wider conflict.”

“One, it’s not clear that the limited and time-bound military escalation Trump is willing to undertake at this point will be enough to change Iran’s calculus,”
 he said.

“Two, it’s hard to imagine these options can degrade Iran’s missile and drone capacity to the point that it cannot effectively close the Strait of Hormuz or further damage the Gulf’s critical energy infrastructure.”

🚨 "Train like your life depends on it. Because God forbid, one day it might." Jordan Salinas posted that two years ago. On Saturday it did.

A gunman opened fire with an AR-style rifle at an In-N-Out Burger in Twin Falls, Idaho on August 1. Three people were killed. Seven more were injured... but the death toll could have been far worse.

Jordan Salinas: a healthcare worker and full-time caregiver for his wheelchair-bound brother, was there. 

He drew his handgun, engaged the shooter and drove him away from the restaurant. The gunman, reportedly shocked by the armed response, fled and later died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound.

Jordan didn't pick up a gun until 2021 after witnessing a shooting himself. That was a turning point for him and he spent five years training. He said he was able to "observe, orient, decide and act." 

He trained for a moment he hoped would never come.

God bless Jordan Salinas and patriots like him who step up in moments like these.
